entries.addendum_before_gate_run: Registered before the gate run on fresh dev_gate seeds (305M-310M, 640 episodes): GA-1/GA-2 unchanged. ALSO REPORTED (not a gate): margin of each learned estimate over the strongest individual simple family (dev: tree depth 2). Dev numbers (builder, 300M seeds, 1,801 instances): sequential GA-1 +.0204 [.0114,.0310] marginal pass, one-shot +.0175 fail; vs tree-depth-2 only +.010-.012. Generator pw-v3; revisions v1 (headroom .0016) and v2 (.0084) documented in portworld.md.
entries.result: REGISTERED GATE RUN (dev_gate 305M, 640 episodes, 2,891 instances, oracle certified 100%): GA-1 FAILS (one-shot +.0057 [.0030,.0087]; sequential +.0058 [.0032,.0088]); GA-2 passes (+.040 [.034,.046]). Best simple (inner-selected; trees d2/d3 per fold) .9544; strong v2 baseline .9460; learned one-shot .9601, sequential .9602; hidden-state oracle .9835 (oracle - best simple only .029). Dev estimate (+.020) did not hold on fresh gate instances.
entries.decision: No generator revision: the hidden-state ceiling above the best simple portfolio is only .029, so GA-1's .02 would require public information to capture >2/3 of hidden-state headroom; revising the generator now to create headroom would be manufacturing. Track A Phase-2 (A2/A3 learned controllers with large margin) not run. (Declines the optional one-revision branch in next.fail; design v1 permits but does not require it.)

entries.settings: octets: 320 for both families (U+C+E descriptive); --hold-relevance not used (cost); B2 first-action replacement residual imbalance accepted and disclosed (17/84 unmatched; <=13/384 per class)
entries.result: Pooled over 5 seed pairs (campaign06_bprimary.py; joint configuration/octet bootstrap), b6_hold_SCE 400 configs, 320 SCE octets. B2-B0: gap regret -1.65 [-6.10,+3.08] (P1 fail; per pair -0.1/+32.4/-25.3/-9.5/-5.7); later-decision acc +.010 [-.002,+.022] (P2 fail); near-miss acc -.085 [-.155,-.005] (P3 fail); false-change +.006. First-decision acc +.075 [.041,.106] (secondary). Broader combination variety at matched volume does NOT improve composition on the untouched S+C+E triple by the registered rule; its first-decision gain is on non-flip units and comes from a higher build rate, with worse balanced (5/5 pairs) and near-miss (4/5) octet accuracy and a large loss after a solved probe: an action-preference change on S∧C inputs, not systematic use of the interacting factors. Descriptive arms (3 pairs vs B0 seeds 30-32): B3, dose2, dose3 pass P1/P2 but fail near-miss (P3); dose1, SUP, LRN pass all three; RAWF passes P1 and P3 (fails P2). CAVEAT: the CI resamples configurations only. Under the independent audit (two-level bootstrap; B0 reference = all five seeds or seeds without s32), only LRN still passes all three: dose1 and SUP fail P3 (near-miss −.067 vs pooled B0), and B3 loses P1. The gap-regret wins of dose1-3/SUP/LRN/RAWF are robust to the B0 reference; near-miss is the seed-fragile endpoint.

entries.causal: on-manifold interventions changing one factor via valid configurations; policy changes only where expected utility changes
entries.result: vs B0 (seeds 30-32): LRN gap -14.9, later +.030, near-miss +.098, false-change -.017 (all 3 pairs same sign for gap/later/near-miss); SUP gap -17.3, later +.051, near-miss -.013 (per pair +.24/-.03/-.25); RAWF (same fuse arch, raw inputs) gap -9.4, later +.001, near-miss +.120. LRN-vs-RAWF isolates the auxiliary derived-quantity heads: later-decision accuracy +.030 (3/3 pairs; concentrated in the first decision of later queries, +.126), gap −5.5 (3/3), false change −.019 (3/3), near-miss −.022 (2/3 pairs negative). LRN's near-miss advantage over B0 is shared by RAWF (+.120) and is therefore a fuse-architecture effect.

entries.trigger: A2/A3 shows headroom over A1 per GA AND >=50% of learned-selector regret localized to value misestimates of candidate methods

entries.hypothesis: A learned public-information method/budget selector beats the best tuned simple portfolio (inner-selected among thresholds, depth<=3 trees, tuned logistic, strong v2 baseline, hand portfolio, cascades) on fresh instances, charging selector compute — a small but real margin (gate estimate +.006)
entries.design: 3 lineages = 3 disjoint training populations from the train range (310M-320M); all selectors (learned one-shot, learned sequential, and every simple family) fit on the lineage's training population, hyperparameters/family chosen on the select range (320M-330M, shared), evaluated once on the untouched confirm range (330M-340M, 640 episodes, shared across lineages; paired)
entries.primary: per lineage: U(learned one-shot) - U(best simple chosen on select range) > 0 with episode-clustered 95% LB > 0, in 3/3 lineages; same reported for sequential; GA-2 analogue vs best single reported
entries.practical_note: a pass establishes a small margin below the registered .02 practical-headroom threshold; it is reported as such, not as meaningful metacontrol headroom
entries.metric_checks: selector feature/inference work charged; oracle certified fraction reported; uncertified instances scored vs UB
entries.result: Confirm population 330M (640 episodes, 2,852 instances, oracle certified .999). Best simple chosen on select = tree_d3 in all 3 lineages. One-shot − best simple: +.0032 [.0006,.0067], +.0025 [.0005,.0046], +.0043 [.0014,.0080]: 3/3 PASS; paired mean +.0033 [.0016,.0055]. Sequential +.0039 [.0021,.0062], 3/3. GA-2 analogue +.035. Learned ~.959 vs tree_d3 ~.956 vs hidden-state oracle .9826. Artifacts: research/results/campaign-06/a-cfsmall (hash-checked). AUDIT (review/a-independent-audit.md): The margin is conditional on the registered selector-charge convention (GBT inference = rounds x depth x models units): it passes 3/3 at zero charge, only 1/3 at 2x selector charge, and reverses (-.010 to -.012, 0/3) if the GBT's 45-output leaf accumulation is charged per output as the logistic's multiply-adds are; the mean margin vanishes at ~2,400-4,000 extra inference units per instance. The registered depth-3 tree used a fixed min_leaf (87) and 16 bins; with min_leaf/bins chosen on the select population (audit, post hoc) one-shot - tree is +.0014 [-.0005,+.0036] / +.0030 [+.0007,+.0053] / +.0023 [+.00002,+.0052] (2/3). The learned one-shot equals a depth-3 tree fit in-sample on confirm (-.0002 [-.0012,+.0008]). ~5% of episodes carry the whole net margin.
entries.interpretation: The registered A-CF-SMALL test passes 3/3 (+.0033 [.0016,.0055]), but the margin is not robust: it fails at 2x selector charge (1/3), reverses under per-output GBT inference charging (0/3), falls to 2/3 against a select-tuned depth-3 tree, and is zero against a depth-3 tree fit in-sample. We read this as no practically or robustly detectable learned-selector advantage over a tuned depth-3 tree portfolio in portworld. A strong simple portfolio captures ~54% of the hidden-state oracle's gain over the best single method and ~86-91% of the gain a cross-fitted learned public-information selector achieves.

entries.hypothesis: Auxiliary heads trained to predict derived decision quantities (LRN) improve later decisions on the untouched S+C+E triple relative to the identical fuse architecture without them (RAWF)
entries.design: fresh initialization seeds 35-39 (5 pairs) for LRN, RAWF, SUP, B0 (same b6_B0 training pool, L1 recipe, final checkpoint, snapshot f5ff2d64 trainer); evaluated on a FRESH S+C+E held-out pool (400 configs, new base in the hold sub-range, never used) and FRESH S+C+E octets (320, new base in the cf sub-range); labels built before any confirm evaluation; no model selection
entries.primary: LRN - RAWF, mean over 5 seed pairs, TWO-LEVEL bootstrap (resample seed pairs, then configurations/octets): Q1 gap regret < 0 with 95% upper bound < 0 and >=4/5 pairs negative; Q2 later-decision accuracy > 0 with 95% lower bound > 0 and >=4/5 pairs positive; Q3 near-miss accuracy not worse by > .02 and false-change rate not higher by > .02 (paired means). SUPPORTED iff Q1 and Q2 and Q3.
entries.secondary: SUP - RAWF (ceiling), LRN - B0, RAWF - B0 with the same statistics; per-seed values always reported
entries.notes: The two-level bootstrap addresses the seed variance the B-ARMS configuration-only CI omitted. Old b6_hold_SCE results are not reused for this test. Fresh pool b6c_hold_SCE at config base 6.42e9 (worlds 6.47e9) and octets at CF base 6.65e9; 6.45e9 was rejected by the builder because it coincides with b6_hold_SCE eval worlds. Evaluated with the b6c-aware tools merged from campaign/e06-bfactc (9795f9a2); trainings use snapshot f5ff2d64.
entries.result: Fresh b6c_hold_SCE (400 configs, base 6.42e9) + 320 fresh SCE octets (6.65e9); seeds 35-39; two-level bootstrap. LRN - RAWF: gap regret -2.65 [-5.87,-0.03] (5/5 pairs negative; RAWF mean 17.09) Q1 PASS; later-decision acc +.018 [+.002,+.034] (4/5 positive) Q2 PASS; near-miss +.105 [+.017,+.212], false-change -.032 [-.056,-.009] Q3 PASS -> SUPPORTED. BUT octet flip-set full-member accuracy (the decisions that require the interaction) is LOWER: -.048 [-.091,-.003] (5/5 pairs), balanced +.025 [-.020,+.077]; first-decision acc +.001. Secondary: SUP - RAWF not supported (near-miss -.108, flip +.109: the supplied-quantity ceiling improves interaction-dependent flips but over-changes near-misses); LRN - B0 supported (gap -6.73 [-12.18,-2.40], later +.020, 5/5); RAWF - B0 not supported (gap -4.09 [-10.04,+1.80]); SUP - B0 fails Q3 (near-miss -.112). Artifacts research/results/campaign-06/b-factc (hash-checked).
entries.interpretation: Auxiliary heads predicting derived decision quantities give a small, seed-robust improvement in held-out regret and later-decision accuracy on the untouched S+C+E triple over the identical architecture without them, and make fewer spurious one-factor changes. They do NOT improve (they slightly worsen) the decisions whose optimum flips only under the full interaction; the gain is better value-sensitive later decisions / conservatism, not demonstrated composition of interacting factors. Supplying exact derived quantities (SUP) does improve flip accuracy (+.109) but at a near-miss cost, so the quantities carry interaction-relevant information that the learned heads do not exploit.
